Identify Area-Restricted Phase (ARP) clusters

Source: R/get.arp.R
get.arp.Rd

Identifies spatial Area-Restricted Phase (ARP) clusters using DBSCAN based on spatial proximity, duration, and state classification proportions.

Usage

get.arp(
  data,
  ids = "ID",
  epsilon,
  minPts = 3,
  time.col = "time",
  state.col = "state",
  pct.state1 = NULL,
  delta.days = NULL,
  group.col = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or an object of class disperseR.

ids

Character. Name of the column containing individual identifiers. Default is "ID".

epsilon

Numeric or named list. Spatial distance threshold for DBSCAN. Can be a single value, or a named list per individual or group.

minPts

Integer. Minimum number of points required to form a cluster in DBSCAN. Default is 3.

time.col

Character. Name of the column containing timestamps (must be POSIXct). Default is "time".

state.col

Character. Name of the column containing behavioral or movement state classifications. Default is "state".

pct.state1

Numeric. Maximum proportion threshold of state 1 points allowed in a cluster. If not provided (NULL), this filter is not applied and a warning is triggered.

delta.days

Numeric. Minimum duration threshold in days for a cluster to be classified as a ARP area. Duration is computed from the first to the last location assigned to the cluster, regardless of intermediate locations. If not provided (NULL), this filter is not applied and a warning is triggered.

group.col

Character. Optional column name used for grouping when epsilon is provided as a named list.

Value

An object of class disperseR containing the updated dataset with cluster assignments, a list of cluster summaries, and list of filtered ARP clusters.

Examples

eps <- get.epsilon(sim_states)
#> Computing a global threshold using all data combined.
arp <- get.arp(sim_states, epsilon = eps, delta.days = 2, pct.state1 = 0.2)
arp$arp_clusters
